title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1981-82 combinatorial description of maps ('cartes') on surfaces. A map is encoded by its set R of flags ('repères'), i.e. the triangles of the barycentric subdivision. The involutions τ0, τ1, τ∞ act on R by reflecting a triangle across its side opposite the vertex of type 0, 1 or ∞. Their products are the rotations ρ0 = τ1τ∞, ρ1 = τ0τ∞, ρ∞ = τ0τ1 (up to inverses).

(1) Top line, ending a definition from the previous page. A finite set with this action is 'spécial' when ρ1 = τ0τ∞ acts without fixed points. Equivalently, every edge has four distinct flags, which is the situation of p.54: 9 flags around a triangle because ρ1² = 1.

(2) Duality. Take an oriented map C. The dual map Č lives on the same surface with the same orientation. Its flags are the same triangles, with types 0 and ∞ exchanged. Swapping two of the three types reverses the cyclic order (0,1,∞), so direct flags become inverse flags and conversely. This gives (9): R+(Č) = R−(C) and R−(Č) = R+(C).

(3) Generalisation. To drop the speciality condition, Grothendieck introduces 'cartes cellulaires' with folded edges ('arêtes pliées'). The data are a surface X, a graph K ⊂ X (drawn in the figure as a tree, whose complement is a disc D(X/K)), and a finite vertex set S ⊂ K. S contains all topological vertices (points of order ≠ 2) and possibly some, but not all, endpoints (points of order 1) of K. An endpoint not in S is the end of a folded edge, i.e. a dangling half-edge whose free end is a type-1 point. The axioms are to be restated in terms of S ⊂ K ⊂ X. Along a folded edge there are only two flags instead of four. The next page makes this precise: r' = τ0 r = τ∞ r, so ρ1 r = r. Folded edges therefore correspond bijectively to fixed points of ρ1 (and univalent vertices to fixed points of ρ0).

Purpose: every finite set with a (transitive) action of the cartographic group, oriented or not, should come from a map. Fixed points of ρ1 must be allowed for this; this feeds the dessins d'enfants / Teichmüller-tower programme.
errors: No mathematical errors. Identity (9) is correct: exchanging the types 0 and ∞ while keeping the surface orientation reverses the cyclic order of the three types, so direct and inverse flags are interchanged.

Small looseness: 'S contains all topological vertices and possibly some endpoints' must be read as 'S ⊇ points of order ≠ 2, and the endpoints not in S are exactly the free ends of folded edges'. This is clarified on the next page.

ideas.what: Speciality condition: ρ1 = τ0τ∞ acts freely on flags, so the set comes from a map without half-edges
ideas.modern_name: Maps whose edge involution is fixed-point-free; maps without free (dangling) edges
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones & Singerman (1978); Tutte, Cori (permutation encoding of maps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the cartographic groups but not this detail

ideas.what: Oriented dual map on the same oriented surface; R+(Č)=R−(C)
ideas.modern_name: Dual map / exchanging black and white vertices with faces; the duality automorphism of the cartographic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler, Poincaré duality); in permutation form Cori, Jones–Singerman

ideas.what: Cellular maps with folded edges (S ⊂ K ⊂ X), in bijection with fixed points of ρ1
ideas.modern_name: Maps with free edges / half-edges (dangling edges); general transitive actions of the triangle group (2,·,·) or of the extended triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones & Singerman, 'Theory of maps on orientable surfaces' (1978); Bryant–Singerman for the non-orientable case
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in Esquisse d'un programme §2 (cartographic groups C2, C2+)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard foundational material on combinatorial maps: flags, the dual map, and free half-edges as fixed points of the edge involution. This was already in Jones–Singerman (1978). It is a careful private write-up, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'σ1=σ0σ∞' should read 'ρ1 = τ0τ∞' (image and next page use ρ1 = τ0τ∞); the line starts 'où maintenant "spéciaux" signifie que…'.
'Γ2^0 ensembles finis spéciaux' — the symbol is probably the cartographic group (C2 or C2^+-ensembles); the reading of the superscript is uncertain.
Figure label reads 'arête repliée'; in the text 'arête pliée'.
Margin: 'les sommets marqués sont marqués en gros, le contour du disque D(X/K) en trait fin, les sommets sur le bord du disque figurés en …'.

'une partie finie V(ens. des sommets) S⊂K' — V/S denotes the same set; the text continues 'qui contient tous les sommets topologiques, et éventuellement certains sommets d'ordre 1 ou points-bords de K'.
Last line: '(au lieu de quatre comme dans le cas précédemment étudié)'.
